title: An extension of quasi-coherent modules is quasi-coherent
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $0\to\mathcal F_1\to\mathcal F_2\to\mathcal F_3\to0$ be a short exact sequence of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. If $\mathcal F_1$ and $\mathcal F_3$ are quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent], then $\mathcal F_2$ is quasi-coherent.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01IE (schemes-lemma-extension-quasi-coherent), applied on an affine open cover (quasi-coherence is local); cf. perfect.tex Section 08CL: QCoh is a weak Serre subcategory

proof.text: Restrict the short exact sequence along all affine-open immersions Spec Gamma(X,U) -> X. The source-library restriction functor preserves limits and colimits, hence short exactness; Mathlib restrictFunctor preserves quasi-coherence of the end terms. The images of these immersions cover X.

For each affine restricted sequence T, global sections is a right adjoint and preserves its kernel. Apply [lem-pc-affine-extension-section-surjectivity] for surjectivity of its final map; therefore Gamma(T) is short exact. To see tilde preserves kernels, the kernel k of a map between tilde modules is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel], hence its counit tilde Gamma(k) -> k is invertible. Lift the kernel fork through full faithfulness of tilde; reflection of limits proves the lifted fork is a kernel, so tilde preserves kernels. As an additive left adjoint it also preserves colimits, and therefore takes Gamma(T) to a short exact sequence.

The counit gives a morphism tilde Gamma(T) -> T of short complexes. Its end components are isomorphisms by quasi-coherence. Mathlib ShortComplex.isIso₂_of_shortExact_of_isIso₁₃ gives an isomorphism on the middle term. Mathlib isQuasicoherent_iff_isIso_fromTildeΓ then gives quasi-coherence on each affine restriction. Its global presentation is obtained by presentationOfIsIsoFromTildeΓ; source-library isQuasicoherent_of_iSup_opensRange_eq_top combines these presentations into quasi-coherence of the original middle term.
